text:
rita: Noticed onboarding sample has massive cold-start latency on Android 14 after app background/foreground transitions. First request after resume takes ~6-8s. Subsequent requests are normal.

rita: Repro: open sample -> make request (fast) -> background app for 30s -> foreground -> make same request -> 6-8s hang before server logs arrival. Happens on Pixel 8 and OnePlus on Android 14.

henry: Could be connection pool eviction timing plus TCP TIME_WAIT reuse. OkHttp's ConnectionPool evicts idle connections after 5 minutes by default, but OS-level behavior and wakelocks can change timings across Android versions. Any logs?

rita: Captured OkHttp event listener logs: shows "connection acquired" then long delay inside route selection/handshake. No DNS delay.

leo: Do you use `.connectionPool(new ConnectionPool())` anywhere in sample? Also check `keepAliveDuration` on custom pools. If app process sleeps, sockets can be RST by network stack and OkHttp needs to recreate TLS handshake which spikes latency.

rita: Sample uses default client. No explicit pool config. Also noticed that if I set `.callTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` the call still waits ~6s and then completes fine; setting `connectTimeout` lower drops the hang but sometimes fails with `SocketTimeoutException` which is not great UX for onboarding.

henry: For onboarding DX I'd prefer bounded connect timeout + optimistic retry on idempotent GETs. Example: `connectTimeout(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` + `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)` but only for GETs. 

leo: Alternatively, reduce pool evict time to keep sockets fresh for short-lived sample flows: `new ConnectionPool(5, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` for sample apps (keeps up to 5 connections for 30s). But this is memory tradeoff and not a default recommendation.

rita: I tried `ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)` as a debug test (no pooling) and the first-request cold start disappeared, but overall latency went up a bit for repeated requests. So it points to pooling+platform closing sockets.

henry: There's also an Android platform change in 14 where underlying libs more aggressively close sockets in background to save power. That might explain device/OS correlation. We should add a note in onboarding docs about background-resume cold starts and suggest best-effort mitigations.

leo: For SDK parity/tests: add a matrix test that backgrounds app for 15/30/60s and measures first-request latency on device farm. If flaky, bump sample to show spinner and recommend `connectTimeout(3s)` + user-facing retry guidance.

rita: For immediate fix in sample PR I propose: 1) set ConnectTimeout=4s, CallTimeout=12s, 2) keep default pooling but add a comment and dev flag to set Pool(5,30s) during local dev, 3) add small runtime check on resume to warm connection: `GlobalScope.launch { client.newCall(Request(GET, /health)).execute() }` to pre-warm TLS.

henry: Pre-warm hack is fine for sample but not for production. Make the sample opt-in and clearly label it. Also add note about HTTP/2 handshakes vs ALPN cost.

ci-bot: CI job created: https://ci.internal/repro/1769998888-1 - device runs scheduled.

rita: I'll open PR with sample changes and docs update to DX onboarding. Also file an internal issue to track a longer-term SDK default recommendation for mobile clients. Thanks for the tips.
